tasks.short: Identify vacancies, recruit candidates, conduct interviews and agree hiring decisions.

steps.what: Compare staffing needs with occupied positions and approved headcount.
Approve the vacancy, budget and hiring priority.
Prepare the role description, advert and interview criteria with the hiring manager.

loop.input: Approved vacancy, role template, pay range and hiring-manager notes.
loop.output: Draft vacancy pack with traceable requirements and interview questions.
loop.check: Check required fields, pay range and unsupported requirements; hiring manager checks relevance.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved requirements return to the recruiter.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover structure; role-specific wording requires interpreting free-text notes.

steps.what: Approve and publish the vacancy.
Read applications and assemble evidence against the agreed criteria.

loop.input: Candidate application and explicit vacancy criteria.
loop.output: Source-linked evidence grid, with missing evidence marked unknown.
loop.check: Validate quotations and source locations; recruiter checks omissions and unsupported inferences.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per application; unreadable material goes to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Applications contain varied free text; fixed fields miss relevant evidence.

steps.what: Choose the interview shortlist using applications and documented criteria.
Arrange interviews and send candidate instructions.
Interview candidates, answer questions and record evidence.
Select the preferred candidate and document the reasons.
Prepare the offer using approved terms and contract templates.
Approve the offer and release it for signature.
Record the accepted offer and pass starter details to HR administration.

tasks.design: Configure vacancy approvals, interview booking, offer templates and starter transfer across the {ATS}, {CALENDAR}, {ESIGN} and {HCM}. Bounded loops draft vacancy packs and extract source-linked application evidence; people shortlist, interview, select and approve offers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful recruitment features often exist, but inconsistent role criteria and disconnected approvals leave manual coordination.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing configuration handles much of the flow. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building missing connectors and constrained document helpers.
tasks.still_hard: Assessing potential, providing accommodations and making fair comparisons remain demanding. GDPR and EU AI Act assessment, meaningful human oversight and consultation under applicable national rules remain necessary.
tasks.human_edge: Build candidate trust, test evidence through conversation and judge trade-offs that a formal criterion cannot settle.

ambition.what: Fortnightly vacancy-priority review against approved headcount and hiring capacity.

tasks.altitude: The HR manager spends less time chasing bookings and assembling paperwork, and more time challenging vacancy priorities and interview quality. Headcount, selection and offer approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Design structured interview criteria and candidate evidence forms.
reach.learn: Job analysis, accessible assessment and evidence-based interview design.

reach.task: Validate vacancy pay ranges before publication.
reach.learn: Pay structures, internal equity and the applicable national transparency rules.

evidence.claim: Approval routing, scheduling, template generation and accepted-offer transfer are established recruitment-system capabilities; local availability varies.
Source-linked application extraction is a proposed bounded helper; its accuracy and time savings require local validation.
Employment screening and selection uses can fall within the EU AI Act's high-risk categories; extraction-only scope needs assessment too.
The digest reports collective age-discrimination proceedings involving screening AI; it supplies no validated savings estimate for this design.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining percentages are design estimates, not measured savings.
The company uses an {ATS} and an {HCM}; configuration is checked before custom development.
Scheduling uses approved messages and candidate-provided availability; exceptions return to the recruiter.
There is no automated candidate ranking, rejection or inference of protected characteristics.
Build ranges cover one recruitment process; access and consultation may overlap engineering work.
unknowns: Which country, collective agreements and employee-representation arrangements apply.
Whether the {ATS} supports the required approvals, scheduling and {HCM} transfer.
Who approves vacancy content, offers and exceptional terms.
Application formats, recruitment volume and current coordination time.
Permitted retention periods and access to candidate documents.
research_questions: For the confirmed country, which hiring, pay-transparency and consultation requirements apply?
Does the proposed evidence-extraction use fall within applicable EU AI Act high-risk requirements?
How reliably does extraction preserve evidence across the languages and formats in scope?
new_work: Review draft vacancy packs and extracted application evidence.
Handle scheduling exceptions and candidate accommodation requests.
Maintain templates, permissions, retention rules and connector mappings.
Sample omissions and inconsistent treatment, including effects on different candidate groups.

tasks.short: Coordinate accident investigations and prepare accurate reports for the insurer.

steps.what: Register the accident notice and identify reporting deadlines.
Collect existing incident, equipment and training records.
Inspect the location and preserve observations and physical evidence.
Interview the affected employee and witnesses, recording their accounts separately.
Reconstruct events, assess conflicting evidence and establish findings within the investigator's remit.
Prepare the insurer report and evidence index.

loop.input: Investigator findings, authorised evidence, reporting checklist and insurer form.
loop.output: Draft report with source references, disputed facts and missing fields.
loop.check: Validate dates, required fields and citations; investigator checks factual fidelity.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair; conflicting facts stay flagged for human resolution.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative evidence must be condensed without changing uncertainty or attributing unsupported causes.

steps.what: Approve the report and the evidence authorised for disclosure.
Submit the approved report through the insurer portal and retain the receipt.
Assess insurer questions and coordinate any approved supplementary response.

tasks.design: Use the {WORKFLOW} to track deadlines and evidence requests, with restricted records in the {DOCS} linked to the {OPS_SYSTEM} and {LMS}. A bounded loop drafts a source-linked insurer report from investigation findings; people investigate, approve disclosure and submit the prepared pack through the {PARTNER_PORTAL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence spans operational records, interviews and insurer-specific forms. Rare cases make broad custom automation difficult to justify.
tasks.enabler_now: Configurable case records, deterministic evidence indexes and narrowly scoped drafting can now be assembled with less engineering effort.
tasks.still_hard: Physical investigation, disputed accounts and disclosure of health information require expertise. Insurer reporting does not replace statutory accident reporting under applicable national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Listen without leading witnesses, preserve uncertainty and distinguish an observation from a conclusion about responsibility.

ambition.what: Post-incident evidence-completeness review for site supervisors.

tasks.altitude: The HR manager spends less time locating records and formatting reports, while remaining available to employees and investigators. Investigation and disclosure authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Maintain a restricted incident case file and evidence index.
reach.learn: Evidence provenance, access controls and retention for sensitive employee records.

reach.task: Support fair witness interviews where disciplinary consequences may follow.
reach.learn: Applicable national representation rights and separation of safety and disciplinary processes.

evidence.claim: Case records, deadline reminders and deterministic evidence indexes can support accident reporting without automating investigation findings.
A source-linked report drafting loop is technically feasible, but the digest provides no accident-reporting product or outcome case.
Health information requires a valid GDPR processing condition, restricted access and purpose-limited disclosure.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining percentages are estimates for a reportable case.
The safety officer leads technical investigation; HR coordinates employee information and insurer reporting.
Emergency response and statutory notifications run separately and are not delayed by this workflow.
The first build prepares submission files; it does not require insurer-portal automation.
Access and consultation ranges include review of sensitive-data handling under applicable national rules.
unknowns: Whether HR, a safety officer or an external investigator owns accident investigations.
Which insurer forms, deadlines and reporting channels apply.
Which national statutory notifications and employee-representation requirements apply.
The lawful basis, health-data condition, retention period and permitted recipients.
Case volume and whether shared case tooling already exists.
research_questions: For the confirmed country, what distinguishes insurer reporting from mandatory authority notifications?
Which evidence and electronic submission formats does the insurer currently accept?
What retention and disclosure requirements apply to the incident records in scope?
new_work: Check drafted reports against investigator findings and original evidence.
Maintain reporting checklists and insurer form mappings.
Review case access, disclosure packs and retention dates.
Handle missing evidence, disputed facts and portal submission failures.

tasks.short: Analyse workforce patterns, investigate personnel problems and recommend changes to HR policies.

steps.what: Define the personnel problem, comparison groups and measures.
Retrieve workforce, recruitment and pay reports for the agreed scope.
Reconcile identifiers, dates, denominators and missing values.
Calculate trends and compare groups, accounting for small samples and workforce mix.
Test possible explanations with managers and employee representatives.
Write policy options, supporting evidence, costs and an evaluation plan.

loop.input: Computed findings, validated hypotheses, policy text and budget constraints.
loop.output: Draft policy options separating observed patterns, possible explanations and proposed tests.
loop.check: Match numerical claims to supplied results; HR manager checks reasoning, feasibility and unsupported causal claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported claims are removed or returned for investigation.
loop.why_not_simpler: The recommendation must connect free-text context with evidence; calculations remain deterministic.

steps.what: Approve a policy change or a limited trial after required consultation.
Record owners, review dates and measures for the agreed intervention.

tasks.design: Scheduled jobs on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconcile authorised extracts from the {HCM}, {ATS} and {PAYROLL}, then publish aggregate measures to the {BI}. A bounded loop drafts evidence-linked policy options in the {DOCS}; approved interventions receive owners and evaluation dates in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Metric definitions, historical records and identifiers differ across systems. Repeated reconciliation consumes time before the difficult explanatory work starts.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable transformations, data checks and dashboard components are cheaper to build. A bounded drafting loop can use computed results without doing the arithmetic.
tasks.still_hard: Association rarely establishes why people leave or struggle. Small groups, missing context, privacy constraints and consultation can limit useful comparisons.
tasks.human_edge: Choose meaningful questions, challenge convenient explanations and negotiate an intervention employees and managers can support.
tasks.altitude: The HR manager shifts from commissioning retrospective reports to testing specific policy hypotheses and reviewing intervention results. Policy and budget approval rights remain with the existing decision makers.

reach.role: compensation, benefits, and job analysis specialist
reach.task: Investigate whether reward patterns contribute to retention problems.
reach.learn: Comparable job groups, pay distributions and confounding factors.

reach.task: Evaluate whether a learning intervention changes the targeted workforce outcome.
reach.learn: Evaluation design, baseline selection and limits of causal inference.

evidence.claim: Deterministic extraction, reconciliation and statistical dashboards can automate report preparation; they do not establish causes.
The supplied automate classification overstates whole-task automation because causal interpretation and policy approval remain human.
The cited study covering 25,000 workers, including HR occupations, reported 2.8% time savings and unchanged earnings and hours; it does not validate this design's estimates.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining percentages are hypotheses for a recurring analysis cycle.
This design uses aggregate workforce analysis rather than individual performance prediction or automated employment decisions.
Minimum group sizes and access controls are agreed before dashboard publication.
The first release covers a small agreed metric set and one intervention evaluation.
Consultation and access estimates include any applicable national employee-representation process.
unknowns: Available historical data, shared identifiers and agreed metric definitions.
Whether headcount, full-time equivalents and leaver categories reconcile today.
Which workforce comparisons have a lawful purpose and sufficient sample size.
Who can approve policy trials and fund their evaluation.
Which country and national consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Which evaluation design can credibly test the chosen intervention at the available sample size?
What privacy-preserving aggregation is suitable for the workforce measures in scope?
For the confirmed country, which consultation requirements apply to the proposed analytics and policy changes?
new_work: Resolve data exceptions and maintain metric definitions.
Review drafted options and check numerical claims against source results.
Monitor group disclosure risk and changes in access permissions.
Maintain intervention baselines and record unsuccessful or inconclusive results.

tasks.short: Administer reward, performance, safety and employee recreation programmes, resolving exceptions and monitoring delivery.

steps.what: Review programme rules, policy changes, deadlines and outstanding issues.
Approve programme changes and budgets after required consultation.
Apply approved compensation parameters and validate their effective dates.
Maintain benefits enrolments against employee choices and eligibility rules.
Resolve pay and benefit exceptions within delegated authority.
Launch performance reviews, assign forms and chase outstanding submissions.
Facilitate calibration and resolve disputed performance assessments.
Assign safety-programme actions and track completion with the safety officer.
Arrange employee activity invitations and collect registrations.
Reconcile programme costs, participation, exceptions and completion reports.
Review programme outcomes and choose corrective proposals.

tasks.design: Configure eligibility, effective dates and review cycles in the {HCM}, {PAYROLL} and {TALENT}; use the {WORKFLOW} for safety actions and activity registrations. Deterministic reconciliation on the {DATA_PLATFORM} feeds the {BI}, while pay configuration, reward exceptions and performance calibration retain specific human approvals.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each programme has different owners, dates and rules. A spreadsheet often ties together otherwise capable systems, while unusual cases interrupt routine administration.
tasks.enabler_now: Most routine work can use existing configuration. AI-assisted coding makes shared validation rules, reports and missing integrations cheaper to deliver without adding a model to every step.
tasks.still_hard: Fair reward exceptions and performance disputes require accountable judgement. Changes to pay, appraisal, staff-data use or monitoring may require consultation or consent under national rules; specialist safety responsibilities remain.
tasks.human_edge: Explain difficult decisions, recognise unequal effects and mediate between consistent rules and legitimate individual circumstances.

ambition.what: Weekly reward-exception review before the payroll cut-off.

tasks.altitude: The HR manager works from a consolidated exception queue and spends more time on reward fairness, calibration and programme outcomes. Existing budget, pay and performance decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Review reward exceptions for consistency across comparable roles.
reach.learn: Reward governance, effective dating and internal-equity analysis.

reach.task: Validate approved compensation changes before payroll processing.
reach.learn: Payroll cut-offs, reconciliation controls and correction procedures.

reach.task: Track safety-training completion and route overdue requirements.
reach.learn: Certification evidence, renewal rules and escalation boundaries.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 records job schemes for pay transparency. This supports structured reward records, not the entire proposed programme workflow.
Eligibility checks, review reminders, action registers and cross-system reconciliations are mainly configuration and deterministic integration work.
The digest identifies Dutch works-council consent categories covering reward, appraisal and employee-data systems; other countries require separate national assessment.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining percentages estimate a recurring administrative cycle across several programmes.
Routine benefit enrolment implements explicit employee choices under approved rules; ambiguous cases stop for review.
No model scores employee performance or recommends individual pay.
Recreation scope covers invitations and registration; supplier bookings follow the purchasing process.
Approved reward exceptions may feed the next compensation-update batch.
Build ranges cover the shared controls and limited programme pilots; wider country coverage requires further rollout.
Consent and access ranges include employee consultation or works-council involvement where national rules require it.
unknowns: Which programmes HR administers directly and which belong to specialist teams.
How benefits eligibility, pay changes and performance cycles are configured today.
Applicable country, collective agreements and employee-representation requirements.
Which decisions the HR manager may approve and which need escalation.
Whether participation records contain health or other sensitive information.
Available interfaces, test environments and payroll parallel-run windows.
research_questions: For the confirmed country, which programme changes require consultation, consent or collective bargaining?
Which existing configuration features can replace the proposed custom components?
What reconciliation and rollback controls are required for effective-dated pay and benefit changes?
new_work: Maintain programme rules, effective dates, templates and access permissions.
Review pay validation reports and resolve eligibility exceptions.
Monitor integration failures, duplicate changes and missed deadlines.
Review aggregate programme outcomes and avoid treating participation as an employee performance measure.

role.altitude: The HR manager spends less of the week assembling records, coordinating routine handoffs and formatting reports. More time goes to candidate conversations, fair exceptions, investigations and evaluating policy choices; formal employment and budget authority changes only through explicit delegation.
reach: Work with compensation and benefits managers on reward fairness and exception governance.
Work with human resources specialists on structured hiring evidence and restricted case records.
Work with labor relations specialists on representation, consultation and fair investigations.
Work with training and development managers on intervention evaluation and safety-training evidence.
skills_to_grow: Translate policies into explicit rules, exceptions and approval boundaries.
Define workforce metrics and distinguish association from causation.
Evaluate source-linked model drafts and detect missing or invented evidence.
Specify integrations, access controls, retention and reconciliation checks.
Apply GDPR, relevant EU AI Act requirements and confirmed national employment rules.
Design and evaluate limited policy trials.
role.ambitious_version: Run an HR improvement service that combines reliable administration with quarterly policy-trial evaluation, fortnightly vacancy prioritisation and weekly reward-exception reviews. Keep accountable people available for consequential decisions and difficult conversations.
